name: Abū al-Ḥasan Hilāl ibn al-Muḥassin ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ṣābiʾ
summary: Secretary and historian of Baghdad, pupil of al-Fārisī and al-Rummānī, author of Rusūm dār al-khilāfa and Tuḥfat al-umarāʾ.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls Hilāl a secretary who pursued letters and heard from Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā al-Rummānī and Abū Bakr ibn al-Jarrāḥ, and quotes al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī that he was truthful.
Of a family of Sabian secretaries, he became a Muslim and served the chancery of Baghdad; he died there in 448/1056.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 423–424
